text.p: Copper prices closed unchanged in LME trade on Friday ahead of a holiday weekend, despite news of an end to a strike at Chile's Escondida mine and a ris ein LME copper stocks.
Other base metals were mixed, with sinc and lead down, aluminium rangebound and nickel rising.
Gold was slightly easier under US$340 an ounce, and while supported around current levels it was seen capped by producer hedging at around US$345 an ounce.
Oil prices continued to edge lower, as rising supply concerns played on the market.
Wheat weakened on an optimistic crop expectations due to improved weather conditions, and some aggressive fund selling.
The CRB index closed down 1.28 at 246.62.

Copper prices settled unchanged on Friday notwithstanding a rise in LME stocks and news that a strike at Chile's Escondida mine ended. The other base metals were mixed, with zinc and lead edging lower while nickel motored above $7,400. Aluminum was tightly rangebound. Volumes were generally light ahead of a U.K. holiday weekend. The London market will reopen on Tuesday, May 6. Three months copper settled unchanged from Thursday's kerb close at $2,360 per tonne, in the top end of the day's $34 range.

Aluminium was just easier at $1,624, down $4, after shadowing copper lower early in the day and then staging a slight recovery. A stock decline of 2,200 tonnes offered little in the way of upwards momentum and trader said the market was technically driven.

Nickel was more buoyant, ending $80 stronger at $7,430, but it was still well within recent ranges. Zinc and lead, however, languished in slightly lower levels for most of the day and finished easier.Zinc was $7 lower at $1,262, after probing support at $1,255.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Friday, on light volumes, with gold market activity dampened this week by the May Day holiday in Europe Thursday and the U.K. bank holiday Monday. COMEX June gold ended Friday off 10 cents at $341.60, after seeing a $342.0-340.90 range. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was just 10,000 lots.
In the bullion market spot gold ended quoted $339.95/45, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $339.65 and the New York close Thursday around $340.15/65.

"Some support seems to be coming into the gold market around current levels, but producer hedging may cap the market above $345.00 an ounce, as Australian gold miners have been active recently given the slide in the Australian dollar gold price," San Francisco-based Mitsui USA bullion dealer, Greg Drury, said.
The gold price in Australian dollars slid to $432.00 an ounce this week, its lowest level for over 10 years.

NYMEX gasoline prices fell sharply Friday after weak crude prices in the last two sessions finally forced funds to take profits in gasoline which had so far bucked declines, dealers said. June gasoline ended 2.11 cents lower at $60.52 a gallon.

June crude ended 31 cents a barrel lower at $19.60, falling 84 cents since April 30. June heating oil ended 1.31 cents a gallon at 53.02 cents. Dealers said crude's weakness reflects rising supplies in the U.S. Gulf Coast which is where the highest demand is due to the concentration of refineries in the area.

A more optimistic outlook for wheat crop production due to improved weather in France, Australia and the U.S. Great Plains plus aggressive selling by key fund trader Refco Inc drove CBOT soft red winter wheat futures to a lower close, traders said. Dry weather in some U.S. Plains areas, most of France and some key wheat areas of Australia had been leading to concerns about potential reductions in the wheat crops. Refco Inc sold eight million bushels of July which helped trigger declines to the day's lows, traders said.

The recirculation of heavy deliveries posted this week on the May contract also weighed on prices. There were 2.820 million bushels of wheat posted Friday for delivery on the May contract amid weak stopping. Wheat closed two to 8-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 7-3/4 at $4.06-1/4. July was down 8-1/2 at $4.16-1/2.
